Ava: Quick heads-up — saw a perf/regression cluster on Mixtral-8B when testing NTK-style RoPE. p50 token latency +12% at seq=8k with our default kernel routing.
Diego: ugh. is this with kernel_selector_v2 enabled? or fallback to scalar kernels?
Ava: kernel_selector_v2 ON. We let it pick between fused-attn (cuda) and fallback-kv. Routing picked the portable fused kernel for some heads.
Sandeep: can you paste the profile trace? nsys / perf output helps.
Ava: pasted below — short excerpt from nsys: ```
[nsys] timeline: memcpy H->D spikes at token 4096..4100
[nsys] kernels: fused_attn_b16_m8: 47.3ms (hot), kv_shard_sync: 34.1ms
[nsys] occupancy: fused_attn has 60% SM occupancy vs expected 85%
```
Gina: interesting — occupancy drop could be due to unacceptable register spilling with NTK scaling factors. Which RoPE variant did you use? linear/NTK/YARN?
Ava: NTK variant, alpha=0.5 (per the prior paper tweak). Also saw a small perplexity bloat on long-context eval (~+0.9 ppl on arXiv subset at 12k).
Diego: timeline suggests KV cache synchronization cost is dominating at long seq. Are we sharding KV across multiple streams?
Ava: yes, we shard KV across 2 GPU partitions for Mixtral-8B in this test. KV sync occurs every 512 tokens by our current heuristic.
Sandeep: that sync interval seems aggressive for NTK. NTK increases effective attention distances; more KV writes per step. Try increasing kv_sync_interval to 1024 or using async KV flush.
Ava: tried kv_sync_interval=1024 locally. p50 improved from 73ms -> 61ms at seq=8k, tokens/sec +18%. But quality: perplexity went +0.2 further (so total +1.1).
Gina: rough tradeoff. Could be that NTK RoPE interacts with kernel tiling shapes that trigger different kernel code paths (e.g., b16 vs b32 matmul kernels). Diego, can we force kernel selection to b32 fused_attn for Mixtral to see if occupancy stabilizes?
Diego: yes, we have a runtime override: ```
{
  "model": "mixtral-8b",
  "kernel_policy": {
    "force": "fused_attn_b32",
    "prefs": ["latency", "no_spill"]
  }
}
```
Diego: simple experiment — force fused_attn_b32 and disable dynamic spilling heuristic.
Ava: ran that. p50 went down to 55ms, tokens/sec +28% vs baseline. Perplexity returned to baseline (within noise). So kernel shape matters a lot.
Sandeep: OK. So kernel selection + kv_sync heuristics both required for NTK. We should codify per-model safe ranges: for Mixtral-8B NTK: prefer fused_attn_b32, kv_sync_interval>=1024, and cap async_shard_count=2.
Gina: add a fallback plan: if dynamic kernel selection chooses portable kernel with occupancy<70% and seq>4k, force b32 kernel and increase cache interval. That should avoid regressions.
Ava: note on batching heuristics: we saw that continuous batching (auto-batch) created micro-batches of 16 with variable seq lengths — leads to kernel fragmentation at 8k. Turning on seq-aware batching (group by length bins of 1k) reduced kernel churn. p50 saved ~6ms.
Diego: good. Any numbers on memory? NTK + b32 increases register usage -> memory compaction issues?
Ava: GPU memory still within limits; peak VRAM +3% but allocator churn decreased with grouped batching.
Sandeep: for Qwen-7B tests, NTK had different behavior — safe up to seq 6k with linear RoPE as fallback beyond that. We should add model-specific rules: Llama-family => linear RoPE default; Mixtral => NTK allowed up to 12k but only with forced kernel b32 and kv_sync>=1024; Qwen => prefer linear beyond 6k.
Gina: I'll draft a runtime policy PR that encodes: kernel preferences, kv_sync defaults, batching bins, and a small regression detector (ppl + latency) to auto-disable NTK per model when eval windows show +0.5 ppl and +10% p50.
Diego: detector thresholds sound reasonable. Implementation note: add a lightweight eval job that runs on a sample prompt set every rollout. Use cached prefix evaluation to avoid large compute.
Ava: attaching quick repro command for the CI job: ```bash
# repro with forced kernel + longer kv sync
runtime-run --model mixtral-8b --seq 8192 --kernel-policy @/tmp/policy.json --kv-sync 1024 --batch-bin 1000
```
Gina: thanks. next steps: 1) PR runtime policy, 2) add CI eval gating (ppl+latency), 3) run full sweep across linear/NTK/YARN variants for Mixture of models (Mixtral/Qwen/Llama). I'll open tickets for each.
runtime-ci-bot: created ticket RUNTIME-2314 with tests: mixtral-ntk-sweep, qwen-linear-longctx, kernel-policy-e2e. :white_check_mark:
Ava: one more observation — when we disabled dynamic KV shard sync for head dims > 64 the regression vanished entirely. Suggest adding head-dim conditional: if kv_head_dim>64 then kv_sync default 1024.
Sandeep: agreed. That matches theory: larger head dims make per-head buffers heavier -> more sync cost.
Gina: perfect. I'll include those heuristics in the PR and include the performance numbers as comments. Thanks team. :rocket:
